scope: Native read-only before/after working-tree patch comparison, private exact-byte simulation and aligned native panes. Editable patch results and full app/distribution objective remain incomplete.

verification.core: 12 cases x four engines = 48 final passing executions (11 real-Git cases and one metadata/parser case per engine). Three new cases: exact text/binary/rename/mode/add/delete forward and reverse before/after bytes; preview keeps HEAD/raw index/worktree; literal wildcard/backslash/tab/newline/Unicode name, exact symlink target bytes and local apply.whitespace=fix policy; stale, unsafe and foreign review refused. Existing selected/whole-patch regressions pass. Final runs additionally reject a patch through an internal parent symlink and preserve its real target bytes.
verification.native: Complete Import Patch receiver passes four engines. Actual hidden comparison text controls show real base/feature bytes with read-only guard, source Merge colors, ruler line numbers, native Find visibility, file selection and addition absence. A real 120-line patch proves linked vertical scrolling and next-difference selection; original long working bytes preserved. Existing Review Patch selected apply/continue/reverse/busy/quit/option-refresh guards and Import Patch context/identity/drop/preview/divider/Find/recovery/stop regressions pass. No main GUI launch or physical inputs.
verification.builds: Unsigned Debug and Store builds pass. Final Debug/NOTICE bundle is stationary during complete four-engine native receiver; Store runs after terminal Core/native/compiler sessions. Source/NOTICE/receiver/tests frozen during live sessions.
verification.bundles: Debug and Store validators, NOTICE comparisons, inventory pin, CSV 3277 records/seven fields, site and whitespace checks pass. Store packaged Git 2.55.0 (11 universal Mach-O files), EditorConfig, IssueRegex and 98 upstream icons audited.

iterations: First Apple Core run failed: opposite-direction numstat also reverses file-record order, so ordinal pairing selected wrong rename/symlink preimage. Independent real-Git probe confirmed ordering; fixed reversal and tightened missing-file error handling. Repaired 12-case Apple run passes, then three other engine runs pass. No native repair iteration.

Intermediate repaired Core Apple run preceded UI edits; other three intermediate Core runs followed UI edits. Core source/tests unchanged across those intermediate runs. Final parent-symlink guard then triggered all four Core reruns, final Debug, complete four-engine native receiver and final sequential Store.

Final filesystem review added explicit parent-symlink rejection for original reads, temporary copies and temporary result reads; real internal symlink-parent patch rejection/preserved target added to existing stale/unsafe case. All 12 cases rerun sequentially on four engines and pass. Debug/native/Store gates repeated after Core change.
limitations: This comparison is read-only; editing/saving patched result, hunk/line application, conflict merge/reject panes, full TortoiseGitMerge parser and source-exact UI behavior remain pending.

Native compare tests use text modification/addition and a long text file; binary/rename/mode/delete/symlink/local policy coverage is Core evidence. Native binary hex preview, dark rendering, physical keyboard/menu/scroll gestures, accessibility and rendered visual comparison remain unverified.

Opposite metadata record-order pairing is verified for tested engines and patch types. Copy/submodule/repeated-path preview and non-UTF-8 per-file selection are not new runtime cases. Per-file argv filtering requires UTF-8 paths.

Private simulation copies only selected operation input/target paths and returns immutable byte snapshots; no user worktree/index/HEAD writes. Preview does not prevent external writers changing originals afterward; application performs fresh checking.
No signed sandbox/Finder deployment or App Store acceptance claim. GitHub auth/CI/push and CUA unavailable from prior evidence, not retried. Full goal remains active.
Parent-symlink checks strengthen private-copy containment; an actual external-writer race was not deterministically injected or globally locked.
